While I was there, a group was sitting at the table not far from me. There were a couple of girls that I thought may have been single, but no eye contact. Plus, group.

Then I went to the bar where I have been hunting (or attempting some reasonable facsimile - I'm still new). I got some eyes from a couple of girls that didn't interest me. I moved in on one, but she ignored my opener, so I just moved away. 1 approach.

Then a group walked in. 4 people, 2 guys, 2 girls. One girl was my type. And I got eyes from her. I tried to motion her over, thinking if she was interested, she might find an excuse to make her way in my direction, but she looked away too quickly. In hindsight that whole tactic seems silly. I got eyes from her again, but didn't approach. And the reason was the group. It held me back. I wasn't sure how to deal with it, so I didn't move in. Again, in hindsight, it seems like such a simple notion:

How are you guys doing tonight? (physical contact with the target, a hand on the arm, or maybe the hip)

Proceed from there based on physical feedback (she moves away, or slightly closer, or some other signal)

Simple! But alas, I beta'd out.

My presence was good, I maintained my space and demeanor. But my actions betrayed me. In a previous post, I mentioned a few pretty ballsy approaches, several with a bachelorette party. And something occurred to me while thinking on that after my performance tonight: I think the reason that I was so gung-ho in the beginning is because I hadn't fully experienced the level of investment that goes into approaches. Now that I do comprehend, my unconscious defenses are working harder. So overcoming them requires more investment than initially.

My demeanor was good tonight. That was the result of visualization in the moment. I was not the lurker, or the scavenger. I was the hunter, and this was my chosen hunting ground. Corny as it looks written out, it helped tremendously to fall back on that whenever I felt my presence waver.

My takeaway from this evening: My biggest blocks right now are mental. I have discovered a particular strategy that seems to work for me, which is visualization. But there is another tactic that I want to employ more often, and that is a phenomenon that I think I read about in a Roosh book, where the subject of our mental focus becomes the item on which we place importance. So, applied to this case, my focus should have been on the signals I received from the girl, or the girl herself - not her group, not the guy she might have been with.

As for my physical presentation, I'm getting my builk back, slowly but steadily. I'm definitely more cut than I was a month ago. My appearance isn't bad, but it could be much better - some new clothes, a nice pair of shoes, and maybe a little bit of input from a stylist of the male variety. Physical is not really an obstacle for me. Mental is the problem.
